inspection_summary: Inspected all 1211 normalized lines, including the abstract, the phase-based derivation of the asymptotic and exact zero equations, conditional counting-saturation argument, objections and regularization remarks, Lambert-W inversion, numerical procedures, GUE and prime-counting diagnostics, final epistemic qualification, references, and technical endnotes. The source is mathematically rich but formula extraction is visibly fragmented, so equation-bearing units remain usable only with explicit scan-verification cautions. Its strongest reusable content is the representation chain from completed-zeta phase to indexed root equations, together with the clearly exposed dependence of the claimed RH consequence on uniqueness/continuity assumptions and solver-conditional numerical evidence.

sections_inspected.label: Front matter and abstract
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: States the indexed-zero equation, counting-saturation claim, Lambert-W approximation, and numerical diagnostics; title and author matter are nonsemantic.

sections_inspected.label: I. Introduction
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Contrasts strip-wide counting with line-restricted zero equations and motivates counting saturation as the proposed RH route.

sections_inspected.label: II.A. Asymptotic equation
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Uses the completed zeta functional equation, polar phase, a boundary prescription for arg zeta, and a selected cosine-phase branch to derive an indexed asymptotic equation and conditional count.

sections_inspected.label: II.B-C. Exact equation and further remarks
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Replaces Stirling asymptotics by the exact Riemann-Siegel theta phase, states the uniqueness-to-RH conditional, and discusses simplicity, discontinuities, regularization, circularity, and multiplicative-factor objections.

sections_inspected.label: III. Lambert-W approximation
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Drops the fluctuating phase term, inverts the mean equation with the principal Lambert-W branch, estimates spacing, and compares the construction with Gram points.

sections_inspected.label: IV. Numerical solutions
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Shows how the arg-zeta fluctuation shifts the mean predictor and describes bracketing and residual checks for the asymptotic equation.

sections_inspected.label: V. GUE statistics
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Defines normalized zero spacings and uses pair-correlation diagnostics to test whether approximate roots retain local fluctuation statistics.

sections_inspected.label: VI. Prime number counting function
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Reviews explicit formulas linking zeros to prime-counting functions and compares reconstructions from mean-only versus phase-corrected ordinates.

sections_inspected.label: VII. Numerical solutions to the exact equation
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Gives a continuation-like decreasing-delta solver and numerical stress cases for the exact phase equation.

sections_inspected.label: VIII. Final remarks and acknowledgments
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Restates the conditional strategy, explicitly disclaims a rigorous proof, summarizes empirical support, and then passes to nonmathematical acknowledgments.

sections_inspected.label: References and technical endnotes
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Mostly bibliography, with two usable qualifications on symmetric phase combinations and branch-aware evaluation of the logarithmic integral.

accepted_units.title: Strip counting versus critical-line counting
accepted_units.why_material: Sets up the central semantic distinction N(T) versus N0(T) and the proposed saturation criterion: a line-restricted count matching the strip count would exclude additional off-line zeros in that range.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the exact Backlund count and the fluctuating arg-zeta term needed to understand why a smooth asymptotic count alone is insufficient.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on extracted formulas (1)-(2), whose fractions and arguments are fragmented; verify them against the retained PDF before formula-level reuse.

accepted_units.title: Individual-root equations are not counting formulas
accepted_units.why_material: Explicitly distinguishes an equation selecting one ordinate for each index from an aggregate counting identity, preventing a superficial equation-shape analogy from doing the mathematical work.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the paper's own defense against deriving the proposed equations directly from known strip-wide counts.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Primarily prose; equation-number references (14), (20), (1), and (2) require the corresponding equation units.

accepted_units.title: Completed-zeta functional symmetry becomes amplitude and phase
accepted_units.why_material: Transforms the functional equation for the completed zeta function into a polar amplitude-phase representation, creating the phase variable from which the indexed conditions are later extracted.
accepted_units.context_note: The physical free-energy analogy is motivational; the reusable mechanism is functional symmetry plus polar decomposition and Stirling expansion.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula-dependent and visibly extraction-damaged around equations (5)-(7); scan verification is required.

accepted_units.title: Boundary phase prescription and selected cosine branch
accepted_units.why_material: Defines arg zeta at a zero by a one-sided horizontal limit, factors the symmetric completed-zeta combination, selects theta=theta-prime with cos(theta)=0, and obtains an integer-indexed transcendental equation.
accepted_units.context_note: The selection of a particular solution from a more general phase condition is a substantive choice, not a consequence to import silently; later saturation claims depend on it.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Core equations (8)-(14) are formula-heavy and some symbols are degraded; the checked prose recovers the mechanism but exact notation needs PDF verification.

accepted_units.title: Unique indexed solutions imply asymptotic counting saturation
accepted_units.why_material: Explains how a well-defined monotone left side with one solution per index yields N0(T), then compares it with the strip-wide asymptotic count to claim saturation.
accepted_units.context_note: The text assumes the boundary arg-zeta term is well-defined and that the indexed equation has a unique solution for every n; neither numerical agreement nor numbering alone discharges that assumption.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on extracted equations (14)-(15) and jump conventions; verify exact constants and limits from the PDF.

accepted_units.title: Exact Riemann-Siegel phase equation
accepted_units.why_material: Replaces the asymptotic gamma phase by the exact Riemann-Siegel theta function and states the exact indexed equation, with the asymptotic formula recovered by Stirling expansion.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the paper's main exactification step and should remain linked to the earlier branch selection and boundary prescription.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Equations (16)-(20) are fragmented in extraction; exact constants, arguments, and limit placement require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Uniqueness of the exact equation is the RH bottleneck
accepted_units.why_material: Makes the logical bottleneck explicit: monotonicity and a unique solution for every index would turn the exact critical-line count into the full strip count and hence imply RH.
accepted_units.context_note: The local arctangent model explains the sign of the delta prescription but does not by itself prove global monotonicity or uniqueness across every jump.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Prose is recoverable; formulas (20)-(21) and local expansion near a zero need PDF confirmation.

accepted_units.title: Zeros as regularized phase-sign discontinuities
accepted_units.why_material: Reframes a simple zero as a sign jump of normalized completed zeta and uses positive delta to smooth the discontinuity so cos(theta)=0 can be assigned at the zero.
accepted_units.context_note: The simplicity conclusion is argued from the selected cosine correspondence; it should not be detached from that premise.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on equation (22) and Figure 1; graphical claims and extracted fractions require the original PDF.

accepted_units.title: Symmetric multiplicative factors and spurious zeros
accepted_units.why_material: Tests whether multiplying zeta by an auxiliary symmetric factor could manufacture off-line zeros and argues that the symmetric combination factors it out, clarifying what the phase construction is intended to detect.
accepted_units.context_note: The claim relies on the stated symmetry and on returning to the original completed zeta factor; endnote [32] supplies an additional qualification about alternative linear combinations.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula extraction is damaged in the transformed-function notation; use the prose mechanism only until verified.

accepted_units.title: Why dependence on arg zeta is not merely circular
accepted_units.why_material: Separates an indexed equation with an intended unique solution from the undifferentiated equation zeta(z)=0 and notes that the phase term can be computed through independent representations.
accepted_units.context_note: This addresses computational circularity but does not establish the asserted uniqueness.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Mostly prose; exact references to equation (14) and arg zeta inherit the formula-verification requirement.

accepted_units.title: Positive delta turns phase jumps into a zero-counting staircase
accepted_units.why_material: Explains that the small positive shift regularizes a discontinuous oscillatory phase and that adding it to the smooth count yields unit jumps at line zeros.
accepted_units.context_note: The staircase observation supports numerical localization; the further inference from line count to all strip zeros remains conditional on the earlier derivation and uniqueness claim.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Uses Figure 2 and formula (15); figure and constants should be checked in the PDF.

accepted_units.title: Lambert-W inversion of the mean zero equation
accepted_units.why_material: Drops the mean-zero fluctuating phase, chooses the real principal Lambert-W branch, and converts an implicit average equation into an explicit index-to-ordinate predictor.
accepted_units.context_note: This is an approximation and starting value, not the claimed exact zero equation; branch selection is justified by seeking positive real solutions.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Equations (23)-(25) are extraction-fragmented, so the algebraic constants and W argument require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: High-index scale and shrinking mean spacing
accepted_units.why_material: Connects the explicit Lambert-W predictor to arbitrarily high indices and derives the familiar leading scale and shrinking consecutive spacing from W's logarithmic asymptotic.
accepted_units.context_note: Large numerical examples illustrate scale rather than prove digit-accuracy claims; the reusable content is the asymptotic relation.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Table I is heavily formula-dependent; exact huge values are not needed for the semantic unit and should be scan-checked if reused.

accepted_units.title: Lambert predictor versus Gram-point search
accepted_units.why_material: Distinguishes an index-specific approximate ordinate from Gram points used as search brackets and explains how the proposed solver starts from the former without relying on Gram's law.
accepted_units.context_note: The source does not establish superior computational complexity; it explicitly frames the goal as justification of the equations rather than an efficiency proof.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Prose is largely recoverable; the Riemann-Siegel formula and sign condition are extraction-sensitive.

accepted_units.title: The fluctuating phase displaces the smooth predictor to a zero
accepted_units.why_material: Shows conceptually how the arg-zeta term supplies local fluctuations missing from the Lambert mean and changes zero-finding into locating a regulated phase jump near the predictor.
accepted_units.context_note: The plotted example and first-zero value are computational illustrations, not independent proof of the global indexed correspondence.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Relies on Figure 3 and equations (14), (24), and (25); exact plotted functions need PDF verification.

accepted_units.title: Bracketing asymptotic roots and checking residuals
accepted_units.why_material: Uses sign alternation and a Lambert-centered interval for Brent root finding, then compares residuals from computed roots with independently available high-precision ordinates.
accepted_units.context_note: Residual agreement tests whether known roots satisfy the equation and whether the numerical implementation is stable; it does not establish completeness or uniqueness.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Tables II-IV carry decimal and exponent extraction risk; retain only after verification against the PDF or computation artifacts.

accepted_units.title: Pair correlation isolates the importance of local phase fluctuations
accepted_units.why_material: Contrasts the smooth Lambert predictor with phase-corrected roots, defines normalized local spacings, and specifies Montgomery/Odlyzko pair-correlation tests at low and high index ranges.
accepted_units.context_note: Agreement is a diagnostic of retained local statistics, not proof that every computed ordinate is a zeta zero or that RH holds.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Equations (26)-(28) are severely fragmented; exact normalizations, sum constraints, and parameter ranges require PDF verification.

accepted_units.title: Low- and high-range GUE agreement
accepted_units.why_material: Records the reported comparison of phase-corrected numerical roots with the GUE pair-correlation curve in two widely separated index windows.
accepted_units.context_note: This is source-reported numerical evidence without preserved code or raw results in the span; it is solver- and sample-conditional.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on Figure 4 and Table V, so quantitative reuse requires the original figure and reproducible computation.

accepted_units.title: Prime-counting reconstruction separates mean from fluctuation
accepted_units.why_material: Reviews Riemann's explicit formulas and uses prime-counting reconstruction as a downstream control comparing smooth Lambert ordinates with phase-corrected roots.
accepted_units.context_note: The comparison is qualitative in the surrounding figure and uses only the first 50 approximations; it demonstrates sensitivity to phase information rather than exact reconstruction.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Equations (29)-(32) and powers x^rho are formula-sensitive; line 959's real-part symbol is degraded and all formulas need scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Successive decreasing-delta solution of the exact phase equation
accepted_units.why_material: Presents a continuation-like procedure: initialize near the Lambert estimate with moderate positive delta, recenter on each solution, and iteratively decrease delta without setting it to zero.
accepted_units.context_note: The method is described operationally but lacks a convergence or uniqueness proof and uses a generic Mathematica root finder.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Prose is clear; equation references and delta magnitudes should be checked against the PDF.

accepted_units.title: Exact-equation checks across Gram-law failure and high precision
accepted_units.why_material: Tests the exact-equation procedure on early zeros, the first stated Gram-law failure, and a high-index high-precision example, then compares with roots computed by other means.
accepted_units.context_note: Substitution of known roots corroborates an identity numerically but cannot prove global exactness, uniqueness, or completeness.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Large decimal tables are extraction-sensitive and source-reported; verify against the PDF and independent computation before numerical use.

accepted_units.title: The source's final conditional claim and proof disclaimer
accepted_units.why_material: Concisely states the claimed chain from exact phase equation through continuity and uniqueness to counting saturation, while explicitly acknowledging that the approach is not a rigorous proof and separating numerical support from proof.
accepted_units.context_note: This qualification controls interpretation of every earlier unit: the numerical diagnostics support the equations empirically but do not discharge the analytic bottleneck.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Mostly prose and robust to extraction; formula numbering links back to verified units.

accepted_units.title: Alternative symmetric phase combinations are constrained
accepted_units.why_material: Endnote [32] checks a generalized coefficient in the symmetric phase combination and reports that the real-imaginary compatibility condition leaves only the symmetric choice.
accepted_units.context_note: This supports the earlier factorization choice but is a local algebraic constraint, not a proof that the selected phase branch captures all zeros.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula-heavy endnote with degraded primes and inequalities; exact derivation requires PDF verification.

accepted_units.title: Branch-aware evaluation of the logarithmic integral
accepted_units.why_material: Warns that numerical evaluation of Li(x^rho) crosses a branch-sensitive complex function and recommends the exponential-integral representation.
accepted_units.context_note: This is a reusable implementation caveat for the prime-counting diagnostic, not evidence for the zero equation.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The integral defining Ei is fragmented; verify its sign, limits, and argument from the PDF.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Phase representation to conditional counting saturation
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The source's core strategy composes functional symmetry, phase decomposition, a boundary-value prescription, an indexed phase condition, and equality of line and strip counts; the decisive unresolved bridge is global existence and uniqueness for every index.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: This synthesis is a map of the source's conditional argument, not a verified RH proof; the selected phase branch and monotonicity assertion require independent analytic justification.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Positive-shift regularization links meaning to computation
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The same positive delta that gives semantic meaning to phase values at discontinuities also supplies a numerical continuation parameter for locating roots of the phase equation.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: Local smoothing and stable numerical continuation do not imply a globally single-valued branch, convergence for all indices, or completeness of the resulting roots.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Mean location versus arithmetic fluctuation
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Lambert W captures the smooth index-to-height scale, while the arg-zeta term supplies local fluctuations needed for reported GUE spacing and sharper prime-counting reconstruction.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The downstream plots are source-reported, finite, and formula/figure-dependent; they show sensitivity to the phase term but do not validate uniqueness or RH.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Numerical corroboration bounded by the analytic bottleneck
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Residual checks, statistical diagnostics, and high-precision examples consistently support the proposed equations on tested roots, while the source itself preserves the distinction between corroboration and proof.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: Testing known or numerically located roots cannot establish that no additional roots exist off the line or that each indexed phase equation has exactly one solution.
